title: 4521-ESP-ANC-00-61-PS001
summary:
- The document is a notice of alternate billing cycle for a solar power project.
- Project details include location, capacity, and thermal energy storage system.
- Vendor responsibilities involve fabricating pipe spools.
- Items not shop furnished include bolts, gaskets, and valves.
- Contract allows alternate billing cycles other than thirty days.
- Pipes and fittings are pre-purchased by Abener Teyma.
- All welding must comply with ASME B 31.3 standards.
- Socketweld joints require visual inspection, not radiographic examination.
- Fabricator is responsible for maintaining cleanliness of piping materials.
- Contract allows alternate billing cycles.
- Vendor responsible for shipping and marking pipe spools.
- Cleaning and painting requirements before shipping.
summary_points: The document is a notice of alternate billing cycle for a solar power project.
Project details include location, capacity, and thermal energy storage system.
Vendor responsibilities involve fabricating pipe spools.
Items not shop furnished include bolts, gaskets, and valves.
Contract allows alternate billing cycles other than thirty days.
Pipes and fittings are pre-purchased by Abener Teyma.
All welding must comply with ASME B 31.3 standards.
Socketweld joints require visual inspection, not radiographic examination.
Fabricator is responsible for maintaining cleanliness of piping materials.
Contract allows alternate billing cycles.
Vendor responsible for shipping and marking pipe spools.
Cleaning and painting requirements before shipping.
Protection of flanged ends during shipment.
Special considerations for carbon steel and stainless steel piping systems.
Fabrication tolerances specified.
Confidential and proprietary information must be handled according to contract terms.
Tolerances for pipe, fitting, and valve ends are specified in the welding procedure.
Linear dimensions have specific tolerances for various piping components.
Angular tolerances for pipe bends must not deviate more than +0.5 degrees.
Closer tolerances on drawings override general specifications.
